subject: Immediate unplanned cache-eviction workaround — action required
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@nimbus-analytics.com>, ops@nimbus-analytics.com
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Jan 2027 02:15:00 -0800
Subject: Immediate unplanned cache-eviction workaround — action required

Hi Maria / Nimbus ops team,

We’ve detected a rapid increase in prefix cache eviction across a subset of hosts serving your account (NIM-analytics-prod) that is causing intermittent 503s for multi-turn generation workloads. This is an unscheduled, short-notice event — we are pushing an emergency workaround now and need a small action from your side to reduce the impact.

What we are doing immediately
- Rolling a temporary cache-policy override to extend per-key TTLs by 30s for the affected pool.
- Applying a conservative batching cap on generation requests to reduce pressure on the KV cache.
- Collecting logs and heap/disk metrics into a forensic bundle (attached).

What we need from you now (5–10 min)
1) If possible, throttle background bulk-embed jobs and high-concurrency re-runs for the next 30 minutes.
2) If you can, add the header `X-Experiment-Tag: low-burst` to any immediate test traffic to opt those requests into the fallback profile.

Impact: Likely to reduce transient 503s and timeouts but may increase latency by ~50–200ms for some requests during the override window.

I’ll update this thread when the override is removed and with a follow-up root-cause summary. We’ve opened PD-45218 and are coordinating with the runtime team. Attachment: eviction_workaround_steps.pdf (step-by-step for ops).

Apologies for the disruption — we recognize this is high-impact and are treating as critical.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@nimbus-analytics.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, ops@nimbus-analytics.com
Date: Tue, 05 Jan 2027 02:22:43 -0800
Subject: Re: Immediate unplanned cache-eviction workaround — action required

Thanks Laura — we’ve paused our nightly batch re-ingest and applied the header on test runs. Seeing fewer 503s in the last 3 minutes. Can you confirm how long you expect the override to remain in place and whether there’s any data retention/consistency risk for in-flight requests?

-Maria
Maria Gonzalez
Head of Infrastructure, Nimbus Analytics

-Markus
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@nimbus-analytics.com>, ops@nimbus-analytics.com
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Jan 2027 17:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Immediate unplanned cache-eviction workaround — action required

Hi Maria — quick update and postmortem next steps.

Summary: The canary patch (hotfix/evict-weight-20270105) was deployed to 5 hosts at 03:00 PST on Jan 5. The override reduced cache-eviction rate by ~78% within 15 minutes; 503s returned to baseline. We expanded to the full pool at 03:25 and removed the temporary TTL override at 04:10. We have collected a forensic bundle and attached the high-level mitigation runbook.

Root cause (preliminary): An unintended interaction between the recent sequence-length prioritization heuristic and a new batching optimizer produced aggressive per-key weight decay under mixed short/long sequences, accelerating eviction for hot prefixes. We’ve opened SUP-7891 to track the deeper code remediation and tests.

Next steps for Nimbus Analytics:
- RFC review: schedule a 30-minute postmortem review with your infra leads and our runtime engineers (proposed: Thu Jan 7, 10:00 PST).
- Verify: we will provide a test harness for your traffic patterns to validate the permanent fix before rolling to all accounts.
- Compensation: we’re preparing a credit note for the impacted window and will share the estimate after internal billing review.

Attachments: collected-logs-20270105.tar.gz, eviction_workaround_steps.pdf
Related: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1a2bEvacWorkaround, JIRA: SUP-7891, PD-45218

Apologies again for the disruption. We’ll follow up with the full postmortem doc and the remediation PR link once merged.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
